Heard Sri G.Venkata Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner, and Sri S.Venkata Sai Nath,
learned Special Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent.

3. The case of the prosecution, succinctly, is that the de facto complainant is studying 2nd year MLT (Medical Laboratory Technology) Course in VIMS College, Vijayawada and she got acquainted with the petitioner for two years.
On the promise of marriage, the petitioner/accused met the de facto complainant physically at the house and in the fields.

Upon coming to know that the petitioner engaged with another girl, the de facto complainant questioned the petitioner about his cheating and de facto complainant consumed pesticide and was admitted to a hospital for treatment and after discharge, the complaint was lodged.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the allegations in the complaint are false.

The petitioner had no physical contact with the complainant and there is no element of fraud from inception to play fraud on the de facto complainant hence, Section 417 IPC does not apply to the facts of the case.

In support of his contentions, he relied upon judgments in the cases of Ansaar Mohammad vs. The State of Rajasthan and another1, Sonu Alias Subhash Kumar vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another2.
5.

sentences.text: The petitioner promised to marry the de facto complainant and had a sexual relationship.
Thus, prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. As seen from the contents of the complaint, the de facto complainant is aged about 20 years.
The de facto complainant and the petitioner have had a relationship for two years.
In Ansaar Mohammad's case, the Apex Court granted pre-arrest bail.

In that case, the de facto complainant was in relationship with the appellant for a period of four years and the Apex Court observed as follows:
"In view of the said fact, the complainant has willingly been staying with the appellant and had the relationship.

Therefore, now if the relationship is not working out, the same cannot be a ground for lodging an FIR for the offence under Section 376(2)(n) IPC.
2022 Live Law (SC) 599 (2021) 18 Supreme Court Case 517 7.

In Sonu's case, the Honble Apex Court while considering the application under Sec 482 Cr.P.C.
to quash proceedings relating to offence under Sec 376 IPC observed as follows:
"There is no allegation to the effect that the promise to marry given to the second respondent was false at the inception.

On the contrary, it would appear from the contents of the FIR that there was a subsequent refusal on the part of the appellant to marry the second respondent which gave rise to the registration of FIR.

On these fact,
we are of the view that high court was in error in declining to entertain the petition under Sec 482 Cr.P.C. on the basis that it was only the evidence at trial which would lead to a determination as to whether an offence established".
8.

The Apex Court considered the judgment in Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs State of Maharashtra3,
wherein it is stated as follows:
"16. Where the promise to marry is false and the intention of the maker at the time of making the promise itself was not abide by it but to deceive the woman to convince her to engage in sexual relations, there is a misconception of fact that vitiates the womans consent.

entities.text: Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs State of Maharashtra3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, a breach of promise cannot be said to be a false promise.
To establish a false promise, the maker of the promise should have had no intention of upholding his word at the time of giving it.
To summarise the legal position that emerges from the above cases, the consent of a woman with respect to sec 375 must involve an active and reasoned deliberation towards the proposed act.
To establish whether the consent was vitiated by a  misconception of fact arising out of a promise to marry, two propositions must be established.
The promise of marriage must have been a false promise, given in bad faith and with no intention of being adhered to at the time it was given.

sentences.text:
The false promise itself must be of immediate relevance or bear a direct nexus to the womans decision to engage in the sexual act."
9.
Thus, to constitute an offence, the womans consent to the sexual activities in a relationship should have been procured by misrepresentation of fact and falsely promising to marry her.
This element of falsehood should be apparent to be present from the very inception of their relationship.
Only then a promise to marry would be construed to be an element of misconception of fact so as to induce the lady to give consent to the sexual proposal of the accused person.

Otherwise, if it is a promise by the accused person at the beginning and later on, due to any unforeseen and compelling circumstances he is not able to keep up the said promise, that would not amount to be a false promise leading to misconception as regards the facts preceding grant of consent and an offence in the eyes of law.
So far as the grant of anticipatory bail is concerned, the law is well settled.
The Honble Apex Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs Stage (NCT of Delhi)4 answered reference after considering the judgement of Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia Vs State of Punjab5.

sentences.text: 10. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner will cooperate with the investigation, and he will also cooperate with the potency test.
He also would submit that the petitioner is a permanent resident of Gokanakonda village and he will not flee away from the village.

11. Thus, considering the expressions of Honble Apex Court in the judgments referred to supra, in the facts and circumstances of this case, this Court is inclined to grant pre-arrest bail to the petitioner.
12. Accordingly, this Criminal Petition is allowed.

The petitioner/accused shall be released on bail in the event of his arrest in connection with Crime No.95 of 2024 of Vinukonda Police Station, Guntur District on condition of furnishing self bond for Rs.25,000/- (Rupees twenty five thousand only)
with two sureties for a like sum each to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer, Vinukonda Police Station, Guntur District.

On release, the petitioner/accused shall appear before the investigating officer concerned twice a week i.e., on every Wednesday and Sunday between 10.00 a.m. and 3 p.m. for (4) four months or till the filing of charge sheet which is earlier.
14.
The petitioner shall not directly or indirectly contact or threaten the witnesses under any circumstances and any such attempt shall be construed as an attempt to influence the witnesses.
The petitioner shall not tamper with evidence and shall cooperate with the investigation;

15. It is made clear that the petitioner shall scrupulously comply with the above conditions and breach of any of the above conditions will be viewed seriously and prosecution is at liberty to move an application for cancellation of the bail.

The expressions, if any, used in the order are for the disposal of this bail application and will not be construed as findings Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
